contents.name: Ch. 1 Section 1f, Proposition 1.65: equivariant images are faithfully flat over reduced homogeneous targets, locally closed in general, and factor through the reduced image
Ch. 1 Section 1f, Orbit Lemma 1.66 and Example 1.67: every orbit of minimum dimension is closed; SL2 acting on A2
Ch. 4 Section 4h, Theorem 4.27 and Lemma 4.28: Chevalley's theorem that every subgroup is the stabilizer of a line, with the exterior-power lemma
Ch. 5 Section 5c, Definition 5.20 and Propositions 5.21-5.22: quotients of G by H via fat subfunctors and their universal property
contents.reason: The page formulates quotients as fppf quotient sheaves after Stacks 39.20.1 and proves representability through the criterion of Lemma 39.20.3, so Milne's fat-subfunctor formulation and its separate universal property are not consumed.

contents.name: Ch. 5 Section 5c, Propositions 5.23-5.25 and Corollaries 5.26-5.27: dimension additivity, the torsor isomorphism G x H = G x_{G/H} G, and faithful flatness of G -> G/H
Ch. 5 Section 5c, Theorem 5.28 and Appendix B: existence of G/H for arbitrary algebraic groups via the fat-subfunctor theorem
contents.reason: The design keeps general arbitrary-group quotient representability gated and asks for M22 Theorem 7.18 only in the smooth affine case; the page makes no claim about the general theorem or about Appendix B.

contents.name: Ch. 7 Section 7a, Theorem 7.1 and Remark 7.2: the fixed-point subscheme X^G
contents.reason: Fixed-point subschemes are not used by any item of this pair: the quotient theorems use orbit maps and stabilizers only, so the fixed-point construction is deferred rather than rebuilt here.

contents.name: Ch. 7 Section 7c, Propositions 7.4-7.6: stability and smoothness of orbits, faithful flatness of the orbit map, and minimal-dimensional stable subschemes are closed
Ch. 7 Section 7d, 7.9-7.10: P^n represents the functor of rank-one direct summands
Ch. 7 Section 7e, Propositions 7.11-7.17: the orbit map is flat and recognizes quotients, and the quotient G/G_o exists as an immersed subscheme
Ch. 7 Section 7e, Theorem 7.18 and Example 7.19: G/H is a separated algebraic scheme for smooth affine G, and GL2 by a line stabilizer is P1
Chapter 7, Example 7.19: line-stabilizer orbit method adapted to the diagonal torus via the ordered pair of coordinate lines; GL2/T is the complement of the diagonal in P1 x P1
Appendix A Sections A.k-A.l, A.68-A.74: flat and faithfully flat morphisms, open fibres, generic flatness, fibre-dimension inequalities, and the constant-dimension criterion

contents.reason: Geometric quotients in Brion's GIT sense and the non-existence examples are the subject of the reductive invariant theory pair AG-ACT-3, not of this scheme-theoretic quotient page.

contents.name: Proposition 66.14.1: finite locally free groupoid schemes with enough affine-contained orbits have scheme quotients over an arbitrary base
contents.reason: The design restricts the quoted Stacks theorem to affine finite locally free equivalence relations, which is Proposition 39.23.9; the general closed-subset condition and arbitrary-base statement are deliberately not claimed on this page.

contents.name: Lemma 66.14.2: free actions of finite locally free group schemes on quasi-projective schemes have fppf torsor quotients
contents.reason: This free-action statement is not needed: the page's counterexample treats a free action of mu_2 on a finite etale scheme through the affine quotient theorem, which already applies there.

contents.name: Lemma 66.14.3: separatedness and quasi-separatedness of the groupoid quotient
